Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

decode

Turn labelled values into text

Stata 

decode x, generate(str_x)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, str_x = decode(x))

Stata reference · R reference

encode

Turn text into labelled categories

Stata 

encode str_x, generate(x)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, x = encode(str_x))

Differs from Stata Character input gets fresh codes from 1 in UTF-8 radix order; NA and empty strings are missing. Locale-specific Stata ordering can differ. Factor input preserves existing indices and all levels.

Stata reference · R reference

label

Label every value of a categorical variable

Stata 

label define gender 1 "male" 2 "female"

R dplyr 

mutate(data, gender = factor(gender, levels = 1:2, labels = c("male", "female")))

In R a labelled categorical variable is usually a factor. Give levels explicitly so each code gets the right label.

Stata reference · R reference

Remove value labels

Stata 

label drop yesno

R haven 

mutate(data, x = haven::zap_labels(x))

Stata reference · R reference

Attach a value label to a variable

Stata 

label values x yesno

R haven 

mutate(data, x = haven::labelled(x, yesno))

Define the labels once, as yesno <- c(No = 0, Yes = 1), then attach them to any variable; factor() is the usual R alternative.

Stata reference · R reference

Label some values only

Stata 

label define x 9 "Unknown" 10 "Refused"

R haven 

mutate(data, x = haven::labelled(x, c(Unknown = 9, Refused = 10)))

haven preserves partial value labels for a round trip to Stata. tab() displays value labels; codebook() reports counts and variable labels rather than value-label mappings.

Stata reference · R reference

2 more examples and alternatives

Show the categories of a variable

Stata 

label list x

R base 

levels(data$x)

For labelled data read with haven, use haven::print_labels(data$x).

Stata reference · R reference

Label a variable

Stata 

label variable x "Variable name"

R labelled 

labelled::set_variable_labels(data, x = "Variable name")

Labels read from Stata files are kept; variables() and codebook() display them.

Stata reference · R reference

notes

Attach a note to a variable

Stata 

notes x: Collected in wave 2

R base 

attr(data$x, "note") <- "Collected in wave 2"

R has no notes system; an attribute or a comment in the script is the usual substitute.
